transcript.answer:
Summary (root cause)
- The 1.4.2 rollout exposed a per-node tuning file (/etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf, mounted as a hostPath) that has max_open_files < 200 on rcabench-worker2. That makes the app mark itself degraded and return 503 on /healthz, so the readiness probe fails and half the pods (the ones scheduled on rcabench-worker2) became NotReady.

Confirmed facts (what I observed)
1. Deployment and rollout
   - Deployment ledger-api in namespace ledger was updated to APP_VERSION=1.4.2 and updatedReplicas=6; availableReplicas=3 / unavailableReplicas=3 (deployment says "MinimumReplicasUnavailable").
2. Pod distribution and readiness
   - 6 pods ledger-api-866db84748-...: three pods on node rcabench-worker2 are NotReady (READY=false) and three on rcabench-worker are Ready (READY=true).
3. Pod events / readiness failures
   - There are repeated events: "Readiness probe failed: Get "http://<pod-ip>:8080/healthz": dial tcp ...: connect: connection refused" initially, followed (for the 1.4.2 pods) with "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503".
4. Application logs from a NotReady pod (ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4)
   - Every 10s the app prints:
     2026-10-07T09:54:03Z ERROR ledger-api accept failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files
     (repeated many times)
   - This is the application intentionally logging an error when it considers itself degraded.
5. The app code (from ConfigMap ledger-code -> ledger_api.py)
   - The process reads /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf via read_limit() and sets state["ok"]=False when the limit read < NEEDED, where NEEDED = 200.
   - When state["ok"] is False the handler returns HTTP 503 for /healthz.
   - The app prints the "Too many open files" message when read_limit() < NEEDED (so the log is emitted by the app when tuning.conf yields a too-small value).
6. Node health
   - Both nodes rcabench-worker and rcabench-worker2 are Ready at the Kubernetes node level (so Kubernetes node condition is not the issue).

Why this points to the hostPath tuning file on rcabench-worker2
- The deployment mounts a hostPath volume at /etc/ledger-tuning (as seen in the pod spec).
- The app reads that file each loop and switches to degraded if max_open_files < 200.
- NotReady pods are all the ones scheduled on rcabench-worker2 (consistent with that node having a tuning.conf with a low value), while pods on rcabench-worker are OK.
=> Strongly indicates /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf differs between nodes; rcabench-worker2 has max_open_files below 200.

Confidence
- High: the application log messages, the app code behavior, the node-specific failure pattern (only pods on rcabench-worker2 failing), and the readiness probe HTTP 503 all line up with the hostPath tuning file causing the app to mark itself degraded.

Immediate actionable mitigations
1. Fast rollback to restore availability
   - Roll back the deployment to the previous revision (1.4.1):
     kubectl -n ledger rollout undo deployment/ledger-api --to-revision=1
   - Verify rollout status:
     kubectl -n ledger rollout status deployment/ledger-api
   - This will immediately restore the previous behavior while you fix the tuning files.

2. Quick per-node fix (if you want to keep 1.4.2)
   - On rcabench-worker2, update /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf to set:
     max_open_files=200
     (or a larger value, e.g. 65536)
   - You can edit live by SSH-ing to the node and editing /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf, or apply a one-off privileged Job/DaemonSet to write the file if you don’t have SSH access.
   - After fixing the file, either restart the affected pods or let the deployment recover:
     kubectl -n ledger rollout restart deployment/ledger-api
   - Verify pods on rcabench-worker2 become Ready and readinessProbe events stop.

Verification commands (what I ran / what I recommend you run)
- List pods + node and readiness (what I used to confirm):
  kubectl -n ledger get pods -o wide | grep ledger-api
- Check events for readiness errors:
  kubectl -n ledger get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 -o wide
- View application logs (I checked these):
  kubectl -n ledger logs ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 -c api --since=15m | grep "Too many open files"
- Inspect the code that reads the tuning file (I fetched ConfigMap ledger-code -> ledger_api.py) to confirm behavior.

Longer-term fixes (recommended)
1. Make the app resilient:
   - Do not treat node-local tuning mismatch as fatal; instead:
     - Read the OS limit via Python (resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE)) and use that value, or
     - Degrade more gracefully (log warning but keep serving if OS FD limit is adequate for current connections).
   - Make NEEDED configurable via env var (APP_REQUIRED_FDS) so it can be tuned per environment.
2. Avoid per-node hostPath divergence for critical app behavior:
   - Prefer a cluster-wide ConfigMap or a consistent mechanism (DaemonSet that writes same file on all nodes) rather than node-local hostPath differences that affect health checks.
3. Add operational protections:
   - Add readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds and failure thresholds so transient differences during startup don't take pods NotReady too quickly.
   - Consider adding health-check backoff and more informative health endpoints (expose the reason in /healthz or /metrics).
4. If the app legitimately needs higher ulimits, set them via node configuration (sysctl/limits.conf) or have an init process ensure ulimit is set; document the requirement in the deployment runbook.

Exact resources and values I used
- Deployment: ledger-api (namespace: ledger), APP_VERSION=1.4.2, replicas=6, availableReplicas=3, unavailableReplicas=3, deployment revision=2.
- Pods: ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4, -cz4wp, -vv6jk are NotReady (all on rcabench-worker2); remaining three on rcabench-worker are Ready.
- App log sample (NotReady pod):
  2026-10-07T09:54:03Z ERROR ledger-api accept failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files
  (repeated)
- ConfigMap ledger-code ledger_api.py extracts max_open_files from /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf and treats limit < 200 as degraded (prints the "Too many open files" message).

If you want, I can (next)
- Try to read the hostPath file contents from a pod on rcabench-worker2 (I can run a short diagnostic pod scheduled on rcabench-worker2 to cat /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf) and show you the exact value found on that node, or
- Prepare a one-line command / job manifest you can apply to patch /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf on rcabench-worker2 without SSH, or
- Prepare a safe PR patch for ledger_api.py to make the behavior more robust and add an env var to set NEEDED.

Which next step do you want me to take?
